guide.title: Guide: how to play sensibly
guide.lead: A short, practical routine: what you can change in a lottery, how to play and track spending, and what to do if you win. No forecasts.
guide.toc.title: Contents
guide.sources.title: Sources
guide.sources.note: The lottery companies' pages were checked on 6 Nov 2026. Terms can change: check your own company's rules before acting.
guide.minute.title: The essentials in a minute
guide.minute.p1: Every combination has the same chance of winning: the jackpot comes up once in 139,838,160 in both games, whichever numbers you pick.
guide.minute.p2: Past draws say nothing about the next one. "Hot" and "cold" numbers were no better than random ones in the check on real draws.
guide.minute.p3: On average a field returns about half its price: in Lotto 6 aus 49, 50% of stakes go to prizes (lotto.de); for EuroJackpot the app's archive gives about 49.86%.
guide.minute.p4: Two things can be changed: who you share a prize with if you win (your choice of numbers) and how much you spend (fields and draws).
guide.minute.p5: If you win: keep the original receipt, check it against the official result and collect only from your own lottery company. The limit is three years, so do not wait.
guide.control.title: What you can change and what you cannot
guide.control.row1.label: Chance of winning
guide.control.row1.text: Jackpot 1 in 139,838,160 for any combination. The chances by class are on the "Odds" screen and match the tables on lotto.de.
guide.control.row2.label: Share of the prize
guide.control.row2.text: If a popular combination wins, more people split the prize. Rare combinations lower that risk but do not change the chance.
guide.control.row3.label: Spending
guide.control.row3.text: The number of fields and draws decides what you spend. The expected return per euro does not grow with it.
guide.control.chance.title: Chance: it does not change
guide.control.chance.body: Each of the 139,838,160 combinations in both games comes up with the same chance. The row 1-2-3-4-5-6 is neither worse nor better than a "nice-looking" random combination. Some win, however small, happens for about 3.14% of EuroJackpot fields and 3.19% of Lotto 6 aus 49 fields (our calculation from the lotto.de tables).
guide.control.share.title: Share of the prize: it changes a little
guide.control.share.body: A class prize is split between all its winners. If many players choose your kind of numbers (dates up to 31, for example), that class has more winners. In the EuroJackpot archive (its whole history, 1,004 draws on 6 Nov 2026), draws where at least 4 of 5 numbers are 31 or lower had more winners than expected in the class "3 main numbers without Euro": an index of 1.088 against 0.901 for draws with at most two such numbers. An index of 1 means players chose the drawn numbers as if at random. The payout per winner in that class was 14.82 € against 17.45 €.
guide.control.share.limits: This tests one class, the most frequent: the jackpot has too few winners to measure, so for the jackpot it is an inference by analogy. It is an association, not a proven cause, and the sample is small. For Lotto 6 aus 49 there is no such test, because its archive has no winner counts. Every combination keeps the same chance of winning.
guide.control.spend.title: Spending: fully in your hands
guide.control.spend.body: Spending depends on the number of fields, draws per week and the price of a field. Example: 4 fields of Lotto 6 aus 49 in each of the two draws of a week, for 52 weeks, make 416 fields and 499.20 € before fees. On average about half comes back, around 249.60 €. The chance of at least one jackpot in a year is 416 in 139,838,160, about 1 in 336,000. The same 416 fields of EuroJackpot cost 832.00 €.
guide.practice.title: A practical routine
guide.practice.s1.title: Set the budget first
guide.practice.s1.body: Choose the game, the number of fields and how many draws a week you play. Work out the year in the "How much per year" calculator on the "Odds" screen and treat that sum as your limit.
guide.practice.s2.title: Choose the combination
guide.practice.s2.body: Generate fields in "Rarely chosen" mode or check your own on the "Check yours" tab. If a strong rule applies, a tip suggests which number to replace.
guide.practice.s3.title: Save the ticket and keep the receipt
guide.practice.s3.body: Press "Save to tickets", buy the ticket and keep the original receipt. For Lotto 6 aus 49 enter the Superzahl from the receipt on the ticket card. The note is a good place for where you bought it and what you paid.
guide.practice.s4.title: Check after the draw
guide.practice.s4.body: Draws: EuroJackpot on Tuesdays and Fridays, Lotto 6 aus 49 on Wednesdays and Saturdays. Once the draw is in the archive, the prize class shows on the ticket card by itself; if the archive lags behind, update the draws or enter the numbers by hand. If you win, check against the official site.
guide.practice.s5.title: Keep track of the year
guide.practice.s5.body: Once a month compare what you bought with the figure from the calculator. If you spend more than planned, cut the number of fields: the choice of combinations does not affect the chance. Ticket notes and the JSON export help you add up purchases.
guide.avoid.title: What to avoid
guide.avoid.a1.title: The gambler's fallacy
guide.avoid.a1.body: "This number has not come up for a long time, so it is due" and "this number comes up often, so it is on a streak" are the same mistake. The balls do not remember earlier draws. The strategy check on real draws showed that "hot" and "cold" numbers are no better than random ones.
guide.avoid.a2.title: "Systems" and paid "forecasts"
guide.avoid.a2.body: Any system picks one fixed combination, and every fixed combination has the same expected number of matches. There is nothing to buy in a "forecast": it cannot change the chance. Only the share of the prize differs between combinations.
guide.avoid.a3.title: Chasing losses
guide.avoid.a3.body: Past spending does not raise the chance of the next stake. Adding fields after a loss raises the expected loss: on every euro about half still comes back on average. The sum you set in advance is the only reliable limit.
guide.avoid.a4.title: Dates and tidy patterns
guide.avoid.a4.body: Birthdays, sequences and lines on the slip are chosen by many, so such a set would probably have to be shared if it wins. This is about the share of the prize, not the chance.
guide.won.title: If you win
guide.won.intro: The routine is based on the pages of lottery companies (WestLotto, Lotto Brandenburg, Lotto Niedersachsen). They differ in the details, so when in doubt call your own, the one where the ticket was bought.
guide.won.receipt.title: 1. Keep the original receipt
guide.won.receipt.body: For anonymous play the receipt is the key proof: without it no payout is made, and a lost one cannot be replaced by the numbers, the time, the place of purchase or witnesses (WestLotto). Put it somewhere safe and make a copy or photo for yourself (Lotto Niedersachsen). If you played with a customer card or online, the receipt is tied to you and is harder to lose (WestLotto).
guide.won.check.title: 2. Check it against the official source
guide.won.check.body: Compare the draw date, the numbers and the Superzahl with the official data: the Lotto 6 aus 49 numbers and quotas on lotto.de, and for EuroJackpot the Gewinnabfrage on eurojackpot.com. The app shows the prize class, but the official result and your lottery company's check of the receipt decide.
guide.won.keep.title: 3. Do not hand out the receipt or the news
guide.won.keep.body: The receipt is a bearer document (Inhaberpapier, Lotto Brandenburg). So do not post a photo of it and do not give it to anyone except the Annahmestelle or the lottery company. Tell as few people as possible about the win and do not name the amount (Lotto Niedersachsen).
guide.won.claim.title: 4. Collect the prize
guide.won.claim.body: Small amounts are paid at the Annahmestelle against the original receipt and an ID: up to 250 € in cash at WestLotto, up to 500 € at Lotto Brandenburg. Above that limit you fill in a form with your bank details and the money arrives by transfer. If you played online, the win is credited to your account automatically (WestLotto).
guide.won.big.title: 5. Large amounts
guide.won.big.body: Above the limit your company sets, payment is by transfer only: the receipt is checked, then the money arrives in your account. At WestLotto a win above 20,000 € counts as a Zentralgewinn and you are informed by letter. Tell your bank about a large transfer beforehand (Lotto Niedersachsen). From 100,000 € the companies offer voluntary support: ask yours what it offers (WestLotto, Lotto Niedersachsen).
guide.won.deadline.title: 6. The time limit
guide.won.deadline.body: The limit is three years. The companies word it differently: Lotto Niedersachsen says "three years to the end of the year" (by law, sections 195 and 199 BGB), WestLotto says "three calendar years" and in its FAQ "three years from the day of the draw". It is safer to count from the draw day and not to wait. After the period an unclaimed win lapses (Lotto Niedersachsen).
guide.won.tax.title: 7. Taxes for a player in Germany
guide.won.tax.body: For someone living in Germany the win itself is not subject to income tax (Lotto Niedersachsen, test.de). Tax arises on income the win produces, such as interest. Giving large sums to relatives can trigger gift tax, Schenkungsteuer (t-online). For a large win, ask a Steuerberater.
guide.won.scam.title: 8. Letters and calls about "contracts"
guide.won.scam.body: The Verbraucherzentrale warns about fake letters from "law firms" demanding payment for an alleged "lottery contract": do not pay and do not reply (11 Dec 2023). A real win is paid out by the lottery company or its Annahmestelle against your receipt.
guide.faq.title: Questions and answers
guide.faq.q1: Is it worth playing many fields?
guide.faq.a1: Each field adds the same chance of the jackpot (1 in 139,838,160) and the same expected loss. Ten fields of Lotto 6 aus 49 cost 12.00 €, about 6.00 € comes back on average, and the jackpot chance is 1 in 13,983,816. Ten fields of EuroJackpot cost 20.00 €, about 9.97 € comes back on average. The chance grows in proportion to the number of fields and so does the spending: the budget decides, not the number.
guide.faq.q2: EuroJackpot or Lotto 6 aus 49: which is better by expected value?
guide.faq.a2: Almost the same. The return per euro is 50% for Lotto 6 aus 49 (lotto.de) and about 49.86% for EuroJackpot from the app's archive, so about 0.60 € from a 1.20 € field and about 1.00 € from a 2 € field. The jackpot chance per field is identical. Per euro spent a Lotto 6 aus 49 field gives 1.67 times as many chances (2 / 1.20), but the EuroJackpot jackpot can reach 120 million € (lotto.de). Choose by what matters more to you: the price of a field or the size of the jackpot. Slip fees are not included.
guide.faq.q3: Is there a best day or a best jackpot?
guide.faq.a3: There is no best day: draws are independent and the chance of a field is the same on any day. The jackpot size does not change the chance; it changes the prize: the jackpot's contribution to a field's expected return is the jackpot divided by 139,838,160, that is 0.86 € at 120 million € and 0.36 € at 50 million € (before sharing). The prizes of the other classes come on top, and if several people win the jackpot, they share it. See the full estimate on the "Odds" screen.
guide.faq.q4: What does a "rarely chosen combination" mean?
guide.faq.a4: It is a combination on which none of the popularity rules apply: no solid run of dates up to 31, no sequence, no line on the slip and no match with past winning numbers. The estimate rests on the studies by Henze (1997) and Simon (1998) and has no percentages. It tells you how often other players choose such a combination, not how often it is drawn.
guide.faq.q5: Is it true that "rare" combinations win more?
guide.faq.a5: No, they win just as often. Only the share of the prize differs: in the EuroJackpot archive, draws where almost all numbers are 31 or lower had more winners in the class "3 main numbers without Euro" (index 1.088 against 0.901) and a lower payout per winner (14.82 € against 17.45 €). For the jackpot there is no direct test; it is an inference by analogy.
guide.faq.q6: Is it better to play the same combination or to change?
guide.faq.a6: The chance per draw is the same: the balls do not remember the past, and a fixed combination neither raises nor lowers it. Something else matters more: if it is birthdays, other people probably choose such a set too, and the prize would be shared if you win.
guide.faq.q7: How much comes back on average?
guide.faq.a7: In Lotto 6 aus 49, 50% of stakes go to prizes (lotto.de): from a 1.20 € field about 0.60 € comes back on average. For EuroJackpot, by the official quotas and stakes in the app's archive (1,004 draws on 6 Nov 2026), about 49.86% went to prizes, so about 1.00 € from a 2 € field. These are averages over many draws; any single year can turn out differently.
guide.faq.q8: Why does the app give no forecasts?
guide.faq.a8: Draws are random and independent: neither frequencies, nor gaps, nor "systems" change the chance. We tested this on real draws: "hot" and "cold" numbers are no better than random ones. So the app offers what can be checked: an honest generator, a popularity estimate, the odds, spending and ticket checks.
